$comment: T-2.49: which line each event is said with, as data (ADR-017). An event's `lines` are voice-script lines (voices.json), said in turn; `cooldown` seconds must pass before the event is said again — by anyone in the squad, or by the same soldier when `scope` is `speaker`; `priority` decides which of two waiting radio lines goes first; `self` is whether your own soldier says it. A squadmate within `radioBeyondM` of you is heard where they stand, dry; beyond it, over the radio treatment — and only one voice is on the radio at a time: another waits up to `radioQueueSeconds` for it, `radioGapSeconds` apart, or is dropped. A soldier never starts a line within `speakerGapSeconds` of their last one ending. A line nobody has recorded yet plays `chirp` — for your own soldier only when `selfChirp` is true (U-007: off, because your own "reloading" chirp buried your own magazine-out; a recorded line of your own plays either way). `sight` is when an enemy is a new contact: seen within `rangeM` by a squadmate's eye, with no one having seen it for `forgetSeconds`, checked every `everySeconds`. A grenade not the squad's within `grenadeWarningM` of a squadmate is warned of; an enemy dying within `killCreditSeconds` of a squadmate's round or blast is theirs to call. U-012: each event has a `route`. `radio` is squad dialogue (as above); `body` is a soldier's own grunt, cry or last breath, heard where the body is and never over the radio; `shout` is an enemy calling out, heard where it stands and said with the enemy's voices. A route's `audibleM` is as far as it carries (the radio route's far squadmates go over the radio instead), `gainDb` trims it, and `placeholder` is what an unrecorded line plays instead — the chirp on the radio; nothing for a body or an enemy, since a chirp there would say 'radio'. `hit` and `hit-grunt`, `down` and `downed-cry` are one moment's words and body sound; `dying` is a soldier's last breath, only when they die (never when they go down); `enemy-engage` is an enemy firing on the squad after `engageQuietSeconds` quiet.
